messages.subject: AKDE of one behavior type
parts:
Hi all, 

I am a beginner in the ctmm package, I wonder if it makes sense to plot a AKDE but only for a specific behavior. I am intersted in spatial distribution of diving behavior from seabirds. I have a high sampling frequency, 1 GPS location every 4min, so I have sequences of dive behavior around 20 points each. But between them the bird is travelling. I think this can cause discontinuities in the path and mess up the analysis, in particular for computing speed. 

My question is: should I consider each dive sequence as a separate file and perform pkde from the UD estimates for each dive sequence, or should I create for each bird a file (despite it is a gap of non diving behavior between dive sequences). 

I hope the question is clear, sorry if my english is not the best I am French :).

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: AKDE of one behavior type
parts:
Hi,

It makes sense to estimate a distribution for a specific behavior. You just have to make sure that the modeled movement behavior can explain the distance traveled during the gaps. If the behavior is slow moving and the location centers are changing between the behavioral segments, then you can expand the time gaps to accommodate that slow moving behavior.

https://groups.google.com/g/ctmm-user/c/g5UDb40gtUQ/m/2JyshES7BAAJ

If you try to estimate a distribution per dive sequence, then I would worry about the effective sample sizes being too small, but you could try.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: AKDE of one behavior type
parts:
Hi Maxime,

You can do a simple comparison of the mean dive speed compared to the distance between dive areas divided by the time gaps to fly between them.

In another species where birds forage on foot, then the mean foraging speed would be very low compared to the distance between foraging patches divided by the time gaps to fly between them, and you really have to make some adjustment (like expanding the time between) to fit one stationary model to that data. In this case, the gap times need to be expanded sufficiently so that the birds could have walked on foot from one patch to another (even though they don't do that).

Best,
Chris
